owner: OS Product (#410). Release owns the adapter, the observer and the workflow; they read this as data.
provenance: every value is an expected value derived from the pinned public sources below, except gitRequirement.genuineSource, which is marked historical context. None is a host fact. An observer or adapter compares current bytes with them and never copies them into any receipt, bundle report or binding

sources.workingTreeCheck: derivation only: apply-os-changes.py patches build/make (agent tray, updater, background control), so the integrated working tree is not this listing; those post-images belong to an integration report
exact: no RoseOS patch or overlay touches it, so every listed path is present with exactly its mode and blob and nothing else is

environment.when: before envsetup and lunch; lunch then exports BUILD_ID_frankel from cmds-for-envsetup.sh into the shell that runs m, which needs it
environment.setByLunchOnly: BUILD_ID_frankel comes only from vendor/google_devices/frankel/cmds-for-envsetup.sh during lunch
environment.why: git reads GIT_* and stops at GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES (the copy root); BUILD_ID_frankel inherited from the caller hides a missing cmds-for-envsetup.sh; TARGET_KERNEL_DIR or USE_STOCK_KERNEL=true switches the kernel directory away from kernelModuleLists.dir and lunch still passes

writer.text: export async function writeVersionCheckFile(config: DeviceConfig, dirs: VendorDirectories, warnOnly: boolean = false) {
template: `  $(${warnOnly ? 'warning' : 'error'} ${deviceName} vendor module is outdated. Run \`adevtool generate-all -d ${deviceName}\` to update it)\n` +

versionCheck.formRule: the error form is necessary, not sufficient. generate-all writes the warning form only with --noVerify, which skips the FileTreeSpec comparison, so a warning-form module is refused. The error form is also written when no comparison ran (generate-all --updateSpec, and collect-state's temporary module) and when the comparison ran against an edited spec (a working-tree change to vendor-specs/, since it reads the spec on disk). So the error form shows only the version, and generatedVendor.observable must still be compared

executes.compare: $(shell) stdout, trailing newline removed, must equal expected.revision exactly

runsIn: lunch: build_build_var_cache runs soong_ui --dumpvars-mode, whose product configuration imports frankel.mk for TARGET_PRODUCT=frankel
m: the same product configuration again (its dumpvars and the main kati run)
versionCheck.withoutGit: git exits non-zero with nothing on stdout, the comparison fails and the error form stops lunch with "frankel vendor module is outdated"

gitRequirement.functionalMinimum: git accepts a directory with a valid HEAD and enterable objects/ and refs/ as a repository, and rev-parse HEAD on a detached HEAD reads no object; so a lunch that passes the check does not show that the Git data is genuine (os/tests/test_frankel_lunch_inputs.py demonstrates it)

genuineSource.basis: repo checks a project out with .git as a link into .repo/projects; observation 41566744429 recorded this link text on the production tree. Historical context, not an expected value and not current state

acceptance: HEAD is exactly revision plus one newline

in the copy, with GIT_* unset and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES at the copy root, git -C vendor/adevtool rev-parse HEAD prints exactly revision, cat-file -t revision is commit and revision^{tree} is rootTree

nothing redirects outside the copy: vendor/adevtool/.git resolves to a directory inside the copy (a gitfile, or a link to one, is refused); rev-parse --absolute-git-dir and --git-common-dir resolve inside the copy root; no objects/info/alternates, commondir or gitdir file exists; every link in the gitdir resolves inside the copy root; every path in the gitdir is on the copy root's filesystem and none is a mount point; no regular file in it has more than one hard link

items 1-3 alone cannot tell a hand-written gitdir from a genuine one: a HEAD file and an object store holding only the commit pass them. The objects are genuine only when they come from the genuine source, either as an approved byte-for-byte copy (genuine-copy) or fetched from the pinned public remote with every publicFetch.acceptance check passing. Object ids are content hashes, git hashes each fetched object as it indexes it, and connectivity at rootTree then shows the store holds the genuine commit and its whole tree

options.status: allowed only under a separate approval with exact paths and bounds; Release owns the mechanism

options.means: GIT_DIR, a gitfile, a link, alternates or any other way of pointing the copy at the production gitdir or object store

options.status: allowed only under a separate runtime approval for its source and bounds; the interface is publicFetch; Release owns the mechanism

options.means: any HEAD, ref, object or gitdir written other than by a genuine copy or by exactly the publicFetch steps

regenerating the vendor module with --noVerify or --updateSpec, a working-tree change under vendor/adevtool (including vendor-specs/ and vendor-skels/), or editing, replacing or removing adevtool-version-check.mk or frankel.mk

publicFetch.basis: Infra's assessment of adevtool_git_missing (2026-11-04): the isolated copy excludes every .git, so lunch needs genuine metadata for this one project. This follows Blazer's git-meta steps (scripts/blazer-build-only.py git_meta_argv and git_meta) with a stricter tree check
publicFetch.target: <copy>/vendor/adevtool/.git: a new directory, created by the attempt inside the isolated copy only, after the copy's own checks; never the source tree
never: any command that reads or writes the working tree (checkout, reset, status, add)
tags or any ref other than HEAD
acceptance: rev-parse --verify revision^{tree} is exactly rootTree (Blazer checks only that it exists)
git fsck --no-dangling --no-progress succeeds: a full check, so every object's hash and every link from the commit are verified (not --connectivity-only)
git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree revision, each NUL replaced by LF, is byte for byte the decompressed sources[vendor/adevtool].listing (its sha256)
shallow is exactly revision plus one newline
no objects/info/alternates and no remote.* key in git config --local --list
publicFetch.establishes: the genuine objects of public commit revision, by content addressing (commit, tree, blobs, each hash-checked); not provenance from the production gitdir, which only genuine-copy shows. Tree equality, a full fsck and working-tree equality are stronger than the functional minimum
publicFetch.cleanup: on any failure, remove only the .git this attempt created; nothing else in the copy, and never anything in the source tree

ceiling.kind: Infra's proposed execution ceiling for the attempt; neither a measured requirement nor a runtime approval

publicFetch.unbound: sourceTree, lunch, policy and integration-report bindings stay unbound; without an approved attempt that passes, the adapter still refuses with adevtool_git_missing

workingTree.rule: every path of sources[vendor/adevtool].listing is present with exactly its mode and blob, and nothing else is, except .git (gitRequirement)

omittedFromCopy.means: the copy leaves out exactly what these pinned .gitignore rules ignore (git check-ignore semantics, from the project root); a tracked path is never omitted

workingTree.why: the product finder prunes only dl/ and vendor-skels/ (finderPrune), so untracked content anywhere else, such as node_modules/, would be scanned at lunch as an unpinned input
workingTree.onUnlisted: refuse, naming every unlisted path found (bounded), so a first run reports what a real tree holds instead of admitting it

environment.why: without a ceiling git searches above the copy, and a parent repository would answer with a foreign HEAD

gitRequirement.otherGit: none: in the pinned public sources nothing else needs .git or a git process for this lunch and Launcher3QuickStepLib (every *.mk and *.bp of the pinned manifest was searched, #410); content the generated vendor module adds beyond its reference is not covered

buildId.rule: with BUILD_ID_frankel unset beforehand (environment.unset): no vendor/*/frankel/cmds-for-envsetup.sh leaves BUILD_ID at the default and frankel.mk stops lunch; more than one waits on stdin (read -s) and then exits the sourcing shell. The variable is exported into the shell that runs m

files.rule: a missing or empty file stops lunch with $(error)
a missing or empty file stops lunch with $(error)
read at lunch with no guard: a missing or empty file does not stop lunch, so an observer checks it is present at this blob

kernelModuleLists.rule: each file states its own rule; dir holds only with TARGET_KERNEL_DIR and USE_STOCK_KERNEL unset (environment.unset)

finderPrune.why: vendor/adevtool/vendor-skels holds an AndroidProducts.mk for 25 devices; without its .find-ignore the product finder would also list a second frankel product

reference.kind: FileTreeSpec: sha256 of every regular file of the module, "dir" for each directory

generatedVendor.verification: generate-all compares the generated module with the spec file on disk only without --noVerify and without --updateSpec, and fails on any difference; the version check is written after that step and is not in the spec. The warning form records --noVerify, but the error form does not record whether a comparison ran or against which spec bytes, so the observer compares observable itself
generatedVendor.observableScope: these five build definitions only; the rest of the module (proprietary files, overlays, sepolicy) is not covered here
generatedVendor.notEstablished: the host's generated bytes, which flags generated them, and whether vendor/adevtool's working tree matched the pin at the time

branchUse: every branch of launcher3-quickstep-lib.json runs this lunch, so each needs versionCheck satisfied by gitRequirement, environment applied and the markers above present; none of this is a bundle report, a policy receipt or evidence about the three contract projects
